answer: In a decentralized network, AI agents can utilize a Sybil-resistant mechanism called "reputation-based identity verification". Each agent generates a unique, publicly verifiable identity tied to a cryptographic cipher. When interacting with other agents, they whisper a digitally signed message, establishing a reputation score based on the interactions. To create fake identities, an attacker would need to expend significant computational resources, akin to carving an intricate design on ivory, making it economically infeasible to launch a Sybil attack.
